terms.title: Terms of Use
terms.intro: Please read these terms before using MAPA. By registering, you agree to them.
terms.p1: MAPA is a portal to apply for medical financial assistance through {{gateway}}. It records and routes your request; it does not itself pay your bill.
terms.p2: Assistance is not guaranteed. Whether you are approved, for how much, and how soon depend on each agency's decision, its budget, and available slots.
terms.p3: MAPA and {{gateway}} never charge a fee — not for registration, your Access Code, or releasing a Guarantee Letter. Report anyone who asks you to pay.
terms.p4: You confirm that the information and documents you submit are true. False information may void your assistance.
terms.p5: Your personal data is handled under the Privacy Notice, in compliance with the Data Privacy Act of 2012 (RA 10173).
terms.p6: Use MAPA honestly: one active request at a time, and do not impersonate another person or misuse the system.

cost.title: Applying is free
cost.body: MAPA will never ask you for payment — not for registration, not for your Access Code, and not for the release of your Guarantee Letter.
cost.warning: If anyone asks you to pay to speed up your approval, they are not from {{gateway}}. Report it to {{gateway}} right away.

eligibility.notCovered: Outpatients treated at the hospital's own dialysis, chemotherapy, pharmacy, laboratory or clinic can apply. Not covered yet: medicines or tests bought outside the hospital. Ask the hospital's social-services office about other assistance.
eligibility.title: Who can apply
eligibility.intro: MAPA is for hospital patients who cannot pay their hospital bill. You do not need to be good with computers — the form is short, and staff can sit with you and help.
eligibility.q1: You have a bill at a participating hospital: you are being discharged with your final bill, were discharged with an unpaid bill, or are treated there as an outpatient.
eligibility.q2: You need help paying it. A social worker looks at your situation after you apply.
eligibility.q3: You are the patient, or a family member filing for them.
eligibility.codeHeading: To file a request, you'll need a Patient Access Code
eligibility.codeBody: It is handed to you in person, in the patient's name, at the social-services office of the hospital you choose. It is never sent by text, email, or social media — and no one online can give you one. You can create your account before you have it.
eligibility.signupNeeds: To sign up you need an email address and a mobile number.

faq.heading: Questions people ask us
faq.intro: If your question isn't here, visit a social-services office — we would rather explain it than have you guess.
faq.q1: Do I need to pay anything?
faq.a1: No. Applying through MAPA is free, from registration to the release of your Guarantee Letter. {{gateway}} staff and MAPA will never ask for a fee, a deposit, or a 'processing charge'. If anyone asks you for money in exchange for approval, report it to the Medical Social Services office right away.
faq.q2: What is a Patient Access Code and how do I get one?
faq.a2: It is a printed code given to you in person at the {{gateway}} office, after a social worker confirms you are a hospital patient with an unpaid hospital bill. The code links your online application to your real hospital record, so it cannot be requested by phone, text, or email. Bring a valid ID and your billing statement.
faq.q3: Can I apply for a family member?
faq.a3: Yes. A spouse, parent, adult child or other representative may file for the patient. This is common when the patient is still confined or can't use a phone. You give your name and relationship to the patient, upload your own valid ID, take a selfie, and confirm that you are allowed to file for them.
faq.a4: It depends on how complete your documents are and on each agency's review and available slots. {{gateway}} works to verify documents and assess your case as quickly as possible, and you can track every step in your account.
faq.q5: Do I have to go to the hospital for an interview?
faq.a5: No. The assessment is done remotely. A social worker reviews your case online and messages you in the app if they need anything. There is no office interview to attend.
faq.a6: Yes. Your data is handled under the Data Privacy Act of 2012 (RA 10173). Your documents and selfie are used only to verify your identity and your need for assistance, and are shared only with the hospital you file with and the funding agencies your request is sent to. You may ask for a copy of your data or ask that it be corrected at any time.
faq.q7: My treatment repeats, like dialysis or chemotherapy. Do I need a new code each time?
faq.a7: Each code is for one request. For recurring care, the hospital can issue one code that covers a course of treatment, for up to about three months. You still file one request at a time.
faq.q8: Can I apply at another hospital?
faq.a8: Yes. One account works at every participating hospital. Get a code from the social-services office of the hospital where the patient is treated, and file your request there.
faq.q9: Which agencies pay for the assistance?
faq.a9: The hospital sends your request to the partner agencies that can help with your case. You don't apply to them yourself. The current partner programs are:

help.title: Help & Support
help.intro: Frequently asked questions about the MAPA {{portal}}.

patientFaqs.q: How do I request medical assistance?
patientFaqs.a: Open Request Assistance, choose the type of help you need (e.g. Hospital Bill), enter the amount, and upload the document required for that type. {{gateway}} reviews it and endorses it to the agencies that can help. You then review your coverage plan, tap Proceed, and complete each agency's requirements.

patientFaqs.q: Where do I get a Patient Access Code?
patientFaqs.a: Patient Access Codes are issued in person by {{gateway}}. Bring a valid ID. The code follows the format {{codeFormat}}.

A Guarantee Letter (GL) is the official document an agency issues when it approves its share of your bill. Present it at the provider to claim the assistance. Each GL shows the date it is valid until, usually 10 days from issue. A request may receive more than one GL when several agencies co-fund it.

patientFaqs.q: How will I know the status of my request?
patientFaqs.a: You'll receive in-app + email notifications at each step — when {{gateway}} endorses your request, when agencies review it, and at each approval. The Request Assistance page shows your coverage plan and how much has been secured toward zero balance.

patientFaqs.q: Do I need to attend an interview?
patientFaqs.a: No. {{gateway}} assesses your case remotely — a social worker reviews your documents and messages you through the app if anything is unclear. If a short live conversation is needed, they send a Google Meet link; there is no scheduled interview to attend.

patientFaqs.q: Do I choose which agencies help me?
patientFaqs.a: No — you submit one request and {{gateway}} routes it to the agencies that can cover it, sometimes splitting it across several to reach a zero balance. You can have one active request at a time.

patientFaqs.q: How do I withdraw my request?
patientFaqs.a: You can withdraw a request while it's still being reviewed by {{gateway}} (before it's endorsed). After it's endorsed to agencies, contact {{gateway}} or the agency through Messages.

whatIsMapa.title: What is MAPA?
whatIsMapa.content: MAPA (Medical Assistance Portal Access) is an online system shared by participating hospitals for medical financial assistance. You file one request with the hospital you choose. Its social-services office checks your documents, assesses your case remotely and endorses it to partner agencies such as DSWD, PCSO and DOH, which can each cover part of your bill. You don't need to line up at each agency's office.

whoCanUse.title: Who can use MAPA?
whoCanUse.content: Any patient of a participating hospital can use MAPA, and anyone can create an account. To file a request you need a Patient Access Code (format: {{codeFormat}}) from the social-services office of the hospital you choose. It is issued in the patient's name and works for one request.

register.title: How do I register?
register.s1: Open the MAPA registration page and enter the patient's full name, birthdate, contact number and address. Signing up for a family member? Tick the box and enter the patient's details.
register.s2: Enter your email address and create a secure password.
register.s3: Already have a Patient Access Code? Enter it and tap Verify — the last name and birthdate must match the hospital's record. No code yet? Leave it blank.
register.s4: Agree to the terms and submit the form.
register.s5: When you are ready to ask for help, choose a hospital, get a code from its social-services office, and file your request.

upload.title: What documents do I submit?
upload.s1: Open Request Assistance — the required documents are listed there as a checklist.
upload.s2: Attach a clear photo or scan of each one (e.g., Valid ID, Billing Statement, Medical Certificate, Barangay Indigency).
upload.s3: For your Valid ID, the app does a quick on-device name check to help confirm it's yours — it never blocks you.
upload.s4: Take a live selfie when prompted; {{gateway}} compares it to your ID to confirm your identity.
upload.s5: Submit. {{gateway}} reviews and verifies your documents before endorsing your request to agencies.
upload.s6: If {{gateway}} marks a document for correction, you'll be notified — re-upload it from your request.
upload.note: Tip: some verified documents carry over to your next requests at the same hospital: your Valid ID and PhilHealth ID for 12 months, and your barangay indigency certificate and doctor's order for 3 months from the date on them. The live selfie, billing statement and charge slip are needed fresh for each request.

apply.title: How do I request assistance?
apply.s1: Choose the hospital that gave you your final bill or treats you as an outpatient, and get a Patient Access Code from its social-services office. It is issued in the patient's name and works for one request. If you entered a code when you registered, it covers your first request.
apply.s2: Open Request Assistance from the sidebar or the bottom tab, and enter the code if you are asked for it.
apply.s3: Say whether the patient is admitted or an outpatient (and which unit), choose the type of assistance, enter the amount from the final billing statement (admitted patients file at discharge) or the unit's charge slip, attach the required documents and take a live selfie. Outpatients attach the doctor's order and the unit's charge slip instead of a billing statement.
apply.s4: Confirm the declaration and submit. {{gateway}} checks your documents, assesses your case and endorses it to one or more agencies that can help cover your bill.
apply.s5: Open Request Assistance to see your coverage plan, then tap Proceed to send it to those agencies.
apply.s6: Complete each agency's requirements and reply to any messages from your social worker.
apply.s7: Once an agency approves, you will receive a Guarantee Letter to claim your assistance.
apply.note: Important: You can have only one active request at a time. Track its progress anytime under My Application.

withdraw.title: Can I cancel or withdraw my request?
withdraw.s1: Open Request Assistance from the sidebar or the bottom tab. Your active request is shown there.
withdraw.s2: Scroll to the bottom of the request.
withdraw.s3: Tap Withdraw Application. A confirmation appears.
withdraw.s4: Tap Yes, Withdraw. The request is closed and can't be reopened.
withdraw.s5: The access code used for it is spent. To file again, get a new code from the hospital's social-services office.
withdraw.note: You can withdraw until {{gateway}} endorses your request to an agency. After that, reply to your social worker in Messages or contact the social-services office.

cofunding.title: What is co-funding? Why do I see multiple agencies?
cofunding.content: MAPA uses a co-funding model. You file ONE request stating your bill and the amount you need. {{gateway}} verifies your documents and assesses your case remotely, then endorses your request to one or more partner agencies (DSWD, PCSO, DOH, AMBaG) that together cover your bill toward zero balance. Each agency makes its own funding decision and issues its own Guarantee Letter for the portion it covers. You never have to apply to each agency separately — {{gateway}} routes the case for you.
cofunding.note: After {{gateway}} endorses your request, you'll see a Coverage Plan listing each agency. Tap Proceed to confirm and start their reviews.

intakeWizard.title: What is the Household Intake Wizard?
intakeWizard.content: After {{gateway}} starts reviewing your documents, you'll be asked to fill a 5-step household form covering your family, income, expenses, and medical situation. This is the factual part of the Unified Intake Sheet — your social worker adds the assessment portion while reviewing your case remotely. They use this to recommend which agencies should fund your request.
intakeWizard.s1: Open Request Assistance and tap the Household Intake link, or go directly to /patient/request/<id>/intake.
intakeWizard.s2: Step 1 — Household: list each family member living with you.
intakeWizard.s3: Step 2-3 — Income and expenses: monthly income, employment, and household expenses.
intakeWizard.s4: Step 4 — Medical: diagnosis, attending physician, hospital case number, estimated cost.
intakeWizard.s5: Step 5 — Review: confirm everything and submit. Auto-save runs every 2 seconds so you won't lose work.
intakeWizard.note: You can save partial progress and return any time before submission. The wizard remembers where you left off.

requestLifecycle.title: What are the stages of my request?
requestLifecycle.content: Your request goes through six stages from submission to fully funded. The progress stepper on My Application shows where you are.
requestLifecycle.submittedDesc: You filed the request. {{gateway}} will start reviewing your attached documents shortly.
requestLifecycle.underReviewDesc: {{gateway}} is verifying your documents. You may be asked to re-upload any unclear or rejected ones.
requestLifecycle.assessmentDesc: A social worker assesses your case remotely — they may message you if anything is unclear — then completes the Unified Intake Sheet. No interview to attend.
requestLifecycle.endorsedDesc: {{gateway}} has routed your request to one or more agencies. Review the Coverage Plan on My Application and tap Proceed to start their reviews.
requestLifecycle.partiallyFundedDesc: At least one agency has approved their portion. Others may still be reviewing — your bill is being progressively covered.
requestLifecycle.fullyFundedDesc: Every approving agency has covered their portion and your bill is at (or near) zero balance. Download each agency's Guarantee Letter and present it at the named provider.

statuses.title: What do the per-agency (slice) statuses mean?
statuses.content: Each agency {{gateway}} endorses your request to gets its own card on My Application. Each card has its own status as the agency processes your portion.
statuses.endorsedDesc: {{gateway}} has routed your request to this agency. The agency hasn't started reviewing yet — you need to tap Proceed on the Coverage Plan first.
statuses.reviewingDesc: You tapped Proceed and the agency is now reviewing whether to fund this portion of your bill.
statuses.awaitingInfoDesc: The agency needs something from you (a clearer document, a missed detail, etc.). You'll see their message and a re-upload prompt.
statuses.approvedDesc: The agency approved a specific amount toward your bill. Their Guarantee Letter is being prepared.
statuses.certDesc: The agency has issued and signed their Guarantee Letter. Download it from My Application and present it at the named provider (e.g., Hospital Billing, Mercury Drug).
statuses.rejectedDesc: This agency couldn't cover its portion. {{gateway}} may re-endorse to another agency, or your overall request may stay partially funded.

download.title: How do I download my Guarantee Letter?
download.s1: Go to My Application from the sidebar.
download.s2: Find your approved application — it shows a green panel with the approved amount, purpose, and the provider it is payable to.
download.s3: Wait until the agency uploads the wet-signed copy. You will receive an in-portal notification when it is ready.
download.s4: Click the thumbnail to view the signed Guarantee Letter, or click Download to save a copy to your device.
download.s5: Present the signed Guarantee Letter (printed or shown on your phone) at the provider named on it (hospital billing, pharmacy, etc.).
download.note: The Guarantee Letter is valid until the date printed on it, usually 10 days from issuance. Use it before then. The named provider may bill the agency directly for the guaranteed amount — you are not responsible for the guaranteed portion.

contact.title: How do I contact the hospital or an agency?
contact.content: Your social worker or an agency will message you in MAPA when they need something, and you can reply in Messages (sidebar or bottom tab). You can't start a new conversation yourself. If you need to reach the hospital first, visit or call its social-services office; once they message you, you can reply there any time.

forgotPw.title: I forgot my password. What do I do?
forgotPw.content: On the Login page, click "Forgot Password?" and enter your registered email address. A password reset link will be sent to your email. Click the link to set a new password. If you did not receive the email, check your spam or junk folder. For further help, contact {{gateway}}.
